FOREWORD

0.
0.1 This Standards Structural Structural

Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Institution on 24 March 1986, after the draft finalized by the Sections Sectional Committee had been approved by the and Metals Division Council. to for

0.2 Aluminium, because of its lightness, strength and better resistance atmospheric corrosion, has gained popularity in structures especially use in hilly areas and in defence establishments.

0.3 A large number of variety of aluminium sections are being produced In order to standardize these sections for their economic in the country. the Committee had formulated Indian Standard series production, covering angles, channels, beams and tee sections for structural use and other applications. 0.4 This Indian Stadard was first formulated in 1966. In this revision alloys with new definitions as covered in IS : 733-1983* have been used apart from the addition of some more commonly used sections. 0.5 In the preparation of this standard the Committee kept in view manufacturing and trade practices followed in the country in this field. 0.6 A code of practice for use of aluminium alloys in structures, namely, IS : 8147-19767 was published which covers provisions for the design of structures ( except bridges and pressure vessels ) using aluminium alloys. 0.7 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordThe number of significant places retained in ance with IS : 2-1960:. the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified ualue in this standard. *Specification for wrought aluminium and aluminium alloys, bars, rods, and sections I for general enaineering nurnoses 1 i third r&ion J. f%ode of prktice f& ke'of aliknium alloys in structures. fRules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ). 3

The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer.
